title: Wave 19 - promoted from rnd: CUDA 13.4's developer-experience changes, re-sourced from NVIDIA
verifier_note: Promotion, not a research swarm. Re-sourced by the R&D seat on 2026-10-20 from NVIDIA's CUDA Toolkit 13.4 release notes (GA, 13.4.1, archived) and the nvcc 13.4 documentation; the rnd entry's livestream-slide claims that neither source states are not loaded. Retrieval against NVIDIA's pages only; no second model family. See verification.md.

research.notes: Promoted from rnd entry 2026-10-07-cuda-13-4-developer-experience, whose claims rested on a livestream slide. Every row here is re-sourced from NVIDIA's CUDA 13.4 release notes or nvcc 13.4 documentation, read by the R&D seat on 2026-10-20; slide-only items are not loaded.

extras.name: CUDA 13.4: memory-pool IPC works on Windows WDDM for stream-ordered allocations
extras.note: CUDA Toolkit 13.4 release notes (GA, versioned 13.4.1), New Features, CUDA Platform: memory-pool IPC is now supported on Windows WDDM systems for allocations made with the stream-ordered allocator. Rig relevance: the RTX 5090 runs under WDDM, so two processes on the rig (a render server and a scorer, say) can share pool-allocated GPU buffers without a host round trip, which was Linux-only before. Untested on the rig.

extras.name: CUDA 13.4: the driver is not bundled with the toolkit (Windows since 13.1, Linux since 13.4)
extras.note: CUDA Toolkit 13.4 release notes, 2.2 CUDA Driver: the NVIDIA driver is no longer bundled with the CUDA Toolkit, on Windows from CUDA 13.1 and on Linux from CUDA 13.4; install it from NVIDIA's driver downloads. Toolkit and driver upgrades are decided separately. On the rig, driver 617.42 with CUDA 13.4 is recorded in wave 18.

extras.name: CUDA 13.4: cuda-checkpoint can write checkpoint state to persistent storage
extras.note: CUDA Toolkit 13.4 release notes, New Features, CUDA Platform: cuda-checkpoint can now write checkpoint state to persistent storage instead of keeping it only in process memory.

extras.name: nvcc 13.4 documents --fmax-errors=<n> and --Wconversion (a narrowing-conversion warning)
extras.note: NVIDIA CUDA Compiler Driver 13.4 documentation, options 4.2.8.7 and 4.2.8.11: --fmax-errors=<number> sets how many errors are emitted before compilation aborts; --Wconversion warns when an implicit numeric conversion may narrow the value (for example long long to int). The documentation does not say these are new in 13.4 or how they apply to device code.
